title: Continuous Livestock Archetypes: A Strategic Framework for Tailored Management Interventions in Dual-Purpose Cattle Farms in the Ecuadorian Amazon
content: Farm typologies commonly assume discrete groups, although structural heterogeneity in Amazonian cattle systems may instead follow continuous gradients. We evaluated whether 164 dual-purpose cattle farms in the Sumaco Biosphere Reserve, Ecuador, were better represented by mutually exclusive types or continuous archetypal configurations, and whether these configurations were economically differentiated. Factor analysis of mixed data, permutation based dimensional retention, clusterability assessment, archetypal analysis, bootstrap resampling, economic validation, and repeated cross-validation were integrated. Two structural dimensions explained 40.1% of inertia and represented livestock intensification and infrastructure, and farm scale and land use; agreement with multiple factor analysis was high (Procrustes² = 0.990). The Gap statistic supported k = 1, providing no evidence for defensible discrete farm groups. Archetypal analysis instead identified three continuous configurations: lower-input, livestock intensification, and large-scale land-use. Farm positions frequently combined these reference configurations rather than showing exclusive membership. Greater affinity to livestock intensification was associated with the highest annual net benefit and pasture opportunity cost, whereas large-scale land-use showed intermediate economic performance. Predictive accuracy remained modest despite lower errors for models based on archetypes. Continuous livestock archetypes provide a screening framework for differentiated management interventions, but farm decisions require current economic, productive, and parcel information.
